subject.title: build(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 14 updates

question: Should this grouped update of privileged GitHub Actions be approved as one supply-chain change after the remaining source review and workflow gates complete?
rationale: The patch changes third-party code executed with repository tokens, registry credentials, API keys, and security-upload permissions, while the protected security label and incomplete Codex contract inspection require explicit human ownership.

options.title: Complete gates, then approve
options.body: Verify the upstream pins and direct Codex contract, require the pending workflow/security checks to finish, and merge the grouped update if the sensitive paths remain healthy.

options.title: Split sensitive action families
options.body: Separate token, Docker publishing, CodeQL, Codex, and ordinary setup-action updates so each security boundary can be validated and reverted independently.

options.title: Pause the refresh
options.body: Leave the existing pins in place until the current CI failures and Codex-source verification gap can be resolved without ambiguity.

recommendation.title: Complete gates, then approve
recommendation.body: Verify the upstream pins and direct Codex contract, require the pending workflow/security checks to finish, and merge the grouped update if the sensitive paths remain healthy.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest visible connection to release and repository automation operation and is already engaged in the PR timeline.
